Count duplicates at each observation

Source: R/duplicate-tally.R
duplicate_tally.Rd

For every value in a vector or data frame, duplicate_tally() counts how often it occurs in the whole input, and reports the count next to the value.

Call audit() on the output for summary statistics.

Usage

duplicate_tally(x, ignore = NULL, colname_end = "n")

Arguments

x

Vector, matrix, or data frame. Blank strings, "NA", and "NaN" count as missing.

ignore

Optionally, a vector of values not to check. Their tally is NA, as is that of missing values.

colname_end

String. Suffix of the tally columns. Default is "n".

Value

A tibble with the columns of x (a value column if x is a vector), each followed by its tally column. It has the class scrutiny_dup_tally, which is recognized by audit().

Details

Values with few characters are often duplicated by chance: in iris, 99% of values have a duplicate. Duplicates are more meaningful when there are fewer values and they have more characters.

Values are compared and returned as strings, so 1 and "1" are duplicates, but 2 and "2.0" are not: 2.0 becomes "2".

Summaries with audit()

audit() on duplicate_tally() output returns summary statistics for each tally column, with a .total row across all of them. It finds these columns by the names that duplicate_tally() gave them, so a renamed one is left out.

See also

  • duplicate_count() for a frequency table.

  • duplicate_count_colpair() for duplicates between pairs of columns.

  • janitor::get_dupes() for duplicate rows.

Examples

duplicate_tally(x = pigs4)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   snout snout_n tail  tail_n wings wings_n
#>   <chr>   <int> <chr>  <int> <chr>   <int>
#> 1 4.73        1 6.88       1 6.09        1
#> 2 8.13        2 7.33       1 8.27        1
#> 3 4.22        2 5.17       3 4.4         1
#> 4 4.22        2 7.57       1 5.92        1
#> 5 5.17        3 8.13       2 5.17        3

duplicate_tally(x = pigs4$snout)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>   value value_n
#>   <chr>   <int>
#> 1 4.73        1
#> 2 8.13        1
#> 3 4.22        2
#> 4 4.22        2
#> 5 5.17        1

pigs4 |>
  duplicate_tally() |>
  audit()
#> # A tibble: 4 × 8
#>   term     mean    sd median   min   max na_count na_rate
#>   <chr>   <dbl> <dbl>  <int> <int> <int>    <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 snout_n  2    0.707      2     1     3        0       0
#> 2 tail_n   1.6  0.894      1     1     3        0       0
#> 3 wings_n  1.4  0.894      1     1     3        0       0
#> 4 .total   1.67 0.816      1     1     3        0       0

pigs4 |>
  duplicate_tally(ignore = c(8.13, 7.57))
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   snout snout_n tail  tail_n wings wings_n
#>   <chr>   <int> <chr>  <int> <chr>   <int>
#> 1 4.73        1 6.88       1 6.09        1
#> 2 8.13       NA 7.33       1 8.27        1
#> 3 4.22        2 5.17       3 4.4         1
#> 4 4.22        2 7.57      NA 5.92        1
#> 5 5.17        3 8.13      NA 5.17        3
